task.description:
Hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's design at lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md. Independently re-derive your verdict from the artefact itself, not from CODE-DESIGNER's own result.summary (which you should treat as a claim to verify, not a fact to copy) -- see core-directives.md's 'Every producing step has a validating step'. Check specifically:
1. Does the design cover every one of ISS-0451's three acceptance criteria (docs/issues/ISS-0451.yaml): AC1 (a persistent-fault test scenario proving Letflow.Supervisor/Repo/Bandit survive), AC2 (documented restart-intensity arithmetic showing the fix tolerates at least one full Pollers-budget-exhaustion cycle), AC3 (no regression to REQ-219's own AC2 boot-order or AC4 single-crash-isolation tests)?
2. Is the arithmetic in the design actually correct? Work it through yourself rather than trusting the doc's own numbers -- re-derive independently whether the chosen top-level restart-intensity value plus the circuit-breaker's trip threshold genuinely prevents an indefinite persistent fault from ever exhausting the top-level supervisor's budget (not merely delaying it by a bounded, finite number of extra cycles).
3. Does the design contain any implementation code (.ex function bodies)? If it names a new module (e.g. a PollersBreaker GenServer), it should specify signatures/@specs/state-shape/callback contracts only -- fail this check if you find an actual function body implementing logic, not just a signature.
4. Is the design unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without having to invent any missing decision (exact config keys, exact state machine transitions, exact backoff schedule values, exact module/file placement)?
5. Does the design explicitly state how REQ-219's own AC2 (boot order: Infrastructure before Pollers) and AC4 (single Pollers-budget-exhaustion event still leaves Infrastructure/Http alone) are preserved, with reasoning you can independently verify against the current code (lib/letflow/application.ex, lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex)?
6. Is the specified regression-test mechanism (how the test keeps the fault persistent, unlike REQ-219's own AC4 test which clears it) concrete enough for TEST-DESIGNER to build without design ambiguity?

This is a hard gate -- FAIL with specific, itemized gaps (per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's validator-fail worked example) if any check above doesn't pass; do not rubber-stamp.
acceptance_criteria: Verdict states explicitly, per ISS-0451 AC, whether AC1/AC2/AC3 are each covered by the design
Verdict states the validator's own independently re-derived arithmetic check result, not a repetition of CODE-DESIGNER's numbers
Verdict states explicitly whether any implementation code was found in the design doc
Verdict states explicitly whether REQ-219 AC2/AC4 preservation reasoning is checked and correct
A FAIL verdict lists every gap by section/line with what must change; a PASS verdict states what was independently re-derived and how
task.regate_note: RE-GATE (iteration 1): CODE-DESIGNER revised lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md per handoffs/WF03-ISS0451-20260904/step-02-code-designer.json's own result.summary -- Pollers' child spec now specifies restart: :temporary in Letflow.Application's children list, so the top-level Letflow.Supervisor is structurally (per Supervisor's own documented :temporary contract) unable to auto-restart Pollers at all; PollersBreaker becomes sole restart authority via explicit Supervisor.restart_child/2 calls from the first :DOWN onward. Re-check specifically: (1) does :temporary actually mean what the design claims -- verify against Elixir's own Supervisor documentation/source, don't take the design's citation at face value; (2) does this genuinely remove the race you found, or introduce a new one (e.g. a window between Pollers exiting and PollersBreaker's restart_child call, during which Pollers is simply down -- is that acceptable, and does the design say so); (3) re-check the revised section 4 arithmetic; (4) re-check that REQ-219 AC2/AC4 preservation reasoning still holds given the child-spec change; (5) re-check section 6's test spec is still concrete given the mechanism change (restart_child instead of terminate_child-then-rely-on-auto-restart). Same rigor as your first pass -- this is not a lighter check because it's a second look.

result.summary: FAIL, rework iteration 2. The design's central §3.4a claim -- that giving Pollers' child spec `restart: :temporary` in Letflow.Application removes the prior iteration's unproven race by construction -- is independently re-verified to be TRUE AS A STATEMENT OF OTP SEMANTICS but FALSE AS APPLIED, because the exact children-list syntax the design specifies (`{Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary}`, §3.4a lines 358-364) does not actually set restart: :temporary on the child spec at all. Verified against this project's own pinned toolchain (Elixir 1.20.3): a 2-tuple {module, arg} entry in a Supervisor children list is normalized by Supervisor.init/2's private init_child/1 as `module.child_spec(arg)` -- i.e. `arg` (here the keyword list `[restart: :temporary]`) is passed as Pollers' start_link init_arg, NOT as Supervisor.child_spec/2 override keys. Live probe: `Supervisor.child_spec({Probe.Worker4, restart: :temporary}, [])` resolves to `%{id: Probe.Worker4, start: {Probe.Worker4, :start_link, [[restart: :temporary]]}}` -- restart is silently absent, defaulting to :permanent, and the keyword list is threaded into the start args instead. The correct override syntax is `Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary)` used directly as the children-list entry (verified: this form correctly resolves to `%{id: ..., restart: :temporary, start: {..., :start_link, [[]]}}`). A second live probe confirms the behavioral consequence: a supervisor started with the design's exact syntax auto-restarted a killed :temporary-intended child (pid1 -> pid2 after Process.exit/2), while the corrected syntax genuinely never restarted it (which_children == [] after exit) -- matching Supervisor's own documented contract at lib/elixir/lib/supervisor.ex lines 194-200 ('the child process is never restarted, regardless of the supervision strategy') and lines 1109-1110 ('for temporary children, the child specification is automatically deleted when the child terminates'). Both doc citations independently confirm check 1 of the regate note (the semantics of :temporary itself are exactly as the design states) -- the defect is that §3.4a's own children-list snippet does not invoke those semantics. Consequence: every downstream claim built on 'Pollers' child spec is now :temporary' is unproven again -- §3.6's 'airtight rather than probabilistic' arithmetic, §4's 'exactly 0, structurally and unconditionally' top-level-consumption claim, §5's AC4-preservation reasoning (which asserts the top level's automatic-restart path 'no longer exists at all'), and §6.2 step 6's test assertion (`Process.whereis(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers) == nil` while :open) all rest on a mechanism that, as specified, still leaves the top-level Supervisor able to auto-restart Pollers exactly as before -- the original rework-iteration-0 race is still live, unchanged, because :temporary was never actually applied. Checks 2-6 of the regate note were also run and are moot pending the fix: (2) the 'new gap' question (a window where Pollers is down and nothing is dispatching restart_child) is well-addressed IF :temporary actually took effect, but doesn't rescue the design as written; (3) §4's arithmetic is internally consistent conditional on the false premise; (4) REQ-219 AC2 boot-order reasoning is untouched by this defect and holds (list order unaffected either way); AC4 preservation reasoning is invalidated by the same root cause -- the existing test (pollers_test.exs lines 152-161) would in fact keep passing unmodified today (contradicting §5's claim that it 'will fail as written'), because the top level DOES still auto-restart Pollers under the design's actual syntax; (5) no .ex implementation code found in the design doc -- signatures/types/state-shape only, this check PASSES; (6) the regression test spec in §6 is concrete but is testing a mechanism (breaker as sole restart authority) that the children-list change as written does not produce.

issues.description: Section 3.4a (lines 358-364): the children-list entry `{Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary}` does not set restart: :temporary on Pollers' child spec. Supervisor.init/2's 2-tuple {module, arg} form passes `arg` as the start_link argument (module.child_spec(arg)), not as Supervisor.child_spec/2 override keys -- verified live against Elixir 1.20.3: this exact syntax resolves to a child spec with no :restart key (defaults to :permanent) and threads `[restart: :temporary]` into Pollers.start_link/1's init_arg instead, which is silently swallowed since Pollers.init/1 ignores its arg today. Fix: use `Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary)` as the children-list entry (or an equivalent explicit map/child_spec/2 form) -- verified live that this corrected form does produce a genuine %{..., restart: :temporary} spec and genuinely suppresses top-level auto-restart on child exit.

Section 3.6/3.7/4 (lines 550-566, 596-663): the 'exactly 0, structurally and unconditionally' top-level-restart-consumption claim and the 'no race to win' framing both depend entirely on §3.4a's syntax actually applying :temporary. Since it does not (see BLOCKER above), the top-level Supervisor still auto-restarts Pollers on every exit exactly as in rework iteration 0, so the ORIGINAL unproven-race gap from gate_history[0] is unresolved, not removed by construction as claimed. Must be re-derived once §3.4a's syntax is corrected -- re-verify the arithmetic still holds under the corrected child-spec form (it is expected to, since the corrected form's underlying OTP semantics were independently confirmed here, but must be re-checked against the corrected snippet, not assumed).

Section 5 (AC4 preservation, lines 688-735): claims the existing pollers_test.exs AC4 test (lines 152-161) 'will fail as written' once Pollers' child spec is :temporary, and requires TEST-DESIGNER to update it. Under the design's actual (broken) §3.4a syntax, the top level still auto-restarts Pollers, so that existing test would in fact keep passing unmodified -- the design's own stated consequence is invalidated by the same root-cause defect. Must be re-derived once §3.4a is fixed: re-confirm whether the corrected child-spec form does make that test's premise false (expected, given the corrected form's confirmed behavior here), and restate this section accordingly.

Section 6.2 step 6 (lines 809-827): the assertion `Process.whereis(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers) == nil` while the breaker is :open is only true if the top level cannot auto-restart Pollers, which requires the corrected :temporary syntax. As specified today, the top level would auto-restart Pollers on the very :DOWN the breaker itself is also reacting to, defeating this observable. Must be re-verified once §3.4a's syntax is corrected.

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- fix §3.4a's children-list syntax to `Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary)` (or equivalent), confirmed live in this gate to correctly apply :temporary semantics per Elixir 1.20.3's Supervisor.child_spec/2 (lib/elixir/lib/supervisor.ex lines 934-943: only the 2-arg child_spec/2 form applies keyword overrides; the children-list {module, arg} 2-tuple form passes arg as the start_link argument instead, per init_child/1 at lines 816-833). Then re-derive/restate §3.6, §3.7, §4's arithmetic and §5/§6.2 step 6's AC4-preservation and test-observable text against the corrected snippet -- this is rework iteration 2 of 3.

gate_history.summary: Design's §4 margin arithmetic ('5 - 2 = 3') assumed PollersBreaker's terminate_child call always beat the top-level Supervisor's own automatic restart-on-exit for the same child crash. Independently re-derived and found unproven: no OTP guarantee that the breaker's monitor-message-then-synchronous-call chain completes before the top-level Supervisor's direct in-process EXIT reaction.
issues: BLOCKER: unproven race in the breaker's termination-vs-automatic-restart ordering, undermining AC2's arithmetic (full text in this run's git history, commit 4e127a7d).
gate_history.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- either restart: :temporary on Pollers' child spec (removes race structurally) or cite an actual OTP ordering guarantee and re-derive the margin.

gate_history.summary: Rework iteration 1's fix (restart: :temporary via a {Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary} children-list entry) correctly diagnoses that :temporary would remove the race by construction, and correctly describes :temporary's OTP semantics (independently confirmed against lib/elixir/lib/supervisor.ex and a live probe on this project's pinned Elixir 1.20.3). But the specific children-list syntax used does not actually apply the :temporary override -- a 2-tuple {module, arg} children-list entry threads `arg` into the child's start_link call, not into Supervisor.child_spec/2's override keys, so the resulting child spec still defaults to :permanent. The original race from iteration 0 is therefore still live under this design as written.
issues: BLOCKER: §3.4a's `{Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary}` children-list syntax does not set restart: :temporary -- verified live that this exact form yields a child spec with no :restart override (Supervisor.child_spec/2's overrides parameter is never invoked by this syntax); the corrected form is `Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary)` used as the children-list entry, confirmed live to work correctly.
BLOCKER: §3.6/§4's arithmetic and 'exactly 0 top-level restarts, structurally' claim depend on the broken syntax and are unproven as a result -- must be re-derived against the corrected snippet.

BLOCKER: §5's claim that the existing pollers_test.exs AC4 test 'will fail as written' is false under the design's actual (broken) syntax -- that test would keep passing, since the top level still auto-restarts Pollers today; must be restated once §3.4a is fixed.
BLOCKER: §6.2 step 6's `Process.whereis(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers) == nil` observable is not reliably true under the broken syntax for the same reason.
gate_history.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- fix §3.4a's children-list syntax to Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary) (or equivalent explicit map form), then re-derive §3.6/§3.7/§4's arithmetic and restate §5/§6.2 step 6 against the corrected mechanism. Rework iteration 2 of 3.
